feedback: Name the creature with the child: 'That's a woodlouse — see the grey armour plates.'
Model calm, curious, caring language for creatures children find 'yucky': 'Worms help the soil — let's put it back gently.'
Celebrate curiosity about less popular creatures as much as butterflies.
activities.intendedInsight: The vocabulary is grounded in real experience, and every minibeast — pretty or not — is interesting and worth naming and caring about.
learnerActions: Go on a real minibeast hunt outdoors (under logs, among leaves, on walls) and find living minibeasts.
Name each creature found, using the field-guide features as a reference.
Record or point to one recognition feature for each creature met.

Observe the 'unloved' creatures (worm, woodlouse, slug, spider) closely — gently handling the ones that are safe to hold, such as worms and woodlice, and observing spiders without handling — using calm, caring language.
activities.title: Bug hunt: name the creatures you actually find
